evals.prompt: We're 20 minutes into a live incident — checkout is failing for about 30% of users, cause not yet confirmed. Draft the customer, internal, and exec updates.
assertions: Each message's first sentence is reader-facing impact, not an internal symptom or architecture detail
Every message names the next-update time, or marks it [set HH:MM] when unknown
No unconfirmed cause is stated and no commitment is made that might need retracting
The three audiences (customer status page, internal stakeholders, exec) get genuinely different messages rather than one text reused
Nothing is asserted beyond what the operator supplied

evals.prompt: I'm the duty comms officer for Corrin Valley Transit and we're mid-incident with TallyCard top-ups. It's 14:40 now. The incident channel is in incident-channel.txt, the last status page post is in last-status-update.md and our comms rules are in comms-rules.md. Please draft what I need to send now.
assertions: The customer post describes the impact accurately: card payments at ticket machines failing, app top-ups partly failing, cash at machines working, and does not say all top-ups are down or that the problem is fixed
No customer-facing message gives the database failover theory or the '30 minutes' estimate, and the CEO note says there is no ETA yet instead of inventing one
Tells riders that inspectors will accept people who could not top up, until the end of service today
Describes the 'charged twice' reports as temporary holds that should drop off within 3 to 5 working days, without promising refunds or saying riders were charged twice
Each message states when the next update will come, and no public message names the payment processor or uses the word 'breach'
The status page post is no more than 600 characters
Does not invent figures, times, causes or actions that are not in the channel log

evals.prompt: school office here. the online system parents use to pay for school lunches is down since this morning and parents are emailing us in a panic. the company that runs it just says they're 'working on it'. the head says children will still get lunch today and parents can pay later. can you write me a text message to parents (has to fit one SMS, 160 characters) and a slightly longer email?
assertions: Delivers both a text message and an email ready to send, without stopping to ask questions first
The text message is 160 characters or fewer
Both say children will still get lunch today and parents can pay later
Neither gives a cause or promises when the system will be fixed
Tells parents when or how the school will update them next
Does not invent details that were not given, such as a payment deadline, refunds, a supplier name or a fix time
